chunks: When their brother Hud said to them: 'Will you not take heed?'

key_terms.أَخُوهُمْ: Their brother, indicating Hud's kinship with his people
key_terms.تَتَّقُونَ: You take heed / You practice God-consciousness (from taqwa)
key_terms.هُودٌ: Hud, a prophet sent to the tribe of Aad

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Hud say to his people in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the title 'Akhuhum' (their brother) underscores Hud’s genuine kinship with the people of 'Ad, emphasizing that prophetic authority is rooted in relatable human connection rather than distant divinity. This verse serves as a foundational model for the concept of *Taqwa* as both an internal spiritual state and an external social responsibility, a theme central to Imam Ali’s teachings in *Nahj al-Balagha*. The call to 'fear God' here is interpreted not merely as dread, but as a conscious awareness of divine presence that guides ethical conduct in daily life.
